title: Orchestrate retention policies and per-tenant encryption compliance reporting
creator: Priya Shah
description: Deliver an end-to-end orchestration component that enforces tenant retention policies across storage backends and emits tamper-evident, signed compliance reports for each tenant. This work integrates KMS/HSM key custody metadata into retention lifecycle events (create, modify, delete), ensures events are residency-tagged, and automates monthly and on-demand audit bundles for customers and internal auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Retention policy engine applies per-tenant retention windows to object lifecycles in S3-like and DB-backed stores according to tenant configuration and region residency constraints.

All key-related lifecycle events (wrap/unwrap, rotate, revoke) are recorded with timestamps, key identifiers, and KMS/HSM provenance metadata into an append-only ledger accessible to the compliance exporter.

Compliance exporter can produce a downloadable, signed audit bundle for a tenant covering a configurable time range containing: retention policy snapshot, key lifecycle events, residency assertions, and retention deletions with object digests.
Audit bundles are signed using an HSM-backed signing key; verification instructions and public verification keys are published to the customer-facing compliance portal.
Automated daily sanity checks run; anomalies (missing provenance, cross-region residency mismatches, unexpected retention truncations) surface as incidents to the security on-call channel.
Performance: orchestration path adds < 30ms median overhead to write-path metadata operations; bulk export generation for a 30-day tenant should complete within 15 minutes.
Feature is behind the 'tenant_compliance_export' flag and covered by unit/integration tests and a small canary rollout to two internal tenants before broad release.
tasks: Design: API for tenant retention config and residency constraints (Confluence design draft)
Implementation: retention-orchestrator service that subscribes to object metadata events and key-provenance log
Integration: KMS/HSM metadata collector plugin to normalize provider responses (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, internal HSM gateway)
Storage: append-only ledger schema in BigQuery with partitioning by tenant and day
Exporter: signed bundle generator that assembles policy, key events, residency assertions, and digests; stores bundles in tenant-specific S3 path
Observability: dashboards for retention application rate, export duration, errors; alert rules for anomalies
Security: HSM signing key lifecycle & rotation plan, implement guarded operations behind KMS agent
Docs & Support: customer-facing compliance guide and internal runbook for support teams
Canary & Rollout: run canary for two low-risk tenants, run manual verification, then incrementally enable for larger tenants
implementation_notes: We will implement a separate service (retention-orchestrator) that consumes metadata change events from the metadata-change bus (kafka) and correlates them with normalized key provenance events produced by the kms-hsm-collector. For performance-sensitive writes, the orchestrator only writes metadata pointers; the heavy work (bundle assembly) runs in an async worker with backoff and concurrency controls. To avoid expanding trusted codebase, HSM signing will be performed by a minimal signing microservice that receives digest manifests and returns signed attestations; signing requests are rate-limited and audited.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: use append-only BigQuery ledger vs. fully on-chain anchoring. Rationale: BigQuery partitioning gives better queryability and performance for exports; on-chain anchoring considered for future immutability guarantees.
Trade-off: synchronous signing on write would increase latency; chosen approach is async signing to keep write-path latency low while ensuring eventual signed evidence availability.
Decision: normalize KMS metadata rather than rely on provider-native payloads to make cross-provider reporting consistent.
Mitigation: when HSM gateway is unreachable, we log a high-severity incident and create a provisional unsigned bundle marked 'pending_signature' that will be reprocessed once signing recovers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation, integration test that simulates tenant object lifecycle with mocked KMS/HSM responses, end-to-end staging run producing audit bundle and verifying signature with published public key. Performance test to validate write-path latency < 30ms overhead and bundle generation time under target for 30-day tenant. Include chaos test where HSM signing is delayed to ensure retry behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy retention-orchestrator and kms-hsm-collector to staging and run nightly exports for test tenants. 2) Canary: enable flag for two internal tenants for 48h, run manual audit verification. 3) Gradual enablement by tenant size: small -> medium -> large over 2 weeks. 4) Monitor retention and export dashboards; rollback immediately on critical anomalies.
observability: Create Grafana panels: 'Retention Rule Application Rate', 'Export Generation Latency P50/P95', 'Unsigned-Provisional-Bundles', 'HSM-Signing-Failure-Rate'. Create PagerDuty escalation if export failures exceed threshold or signing subsystem reports >5% error rate.
